note: RFC 4271 Section 9.2: "Any routes in the Loc-RIB marked as unfeasible SHALL be removed." First judgement 2026-10-26 by an independent auditor. Positive TestLocRIBMirror (plugins/rib/rfc4271_rib_bestchange_test.go): after the only route is removed from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision re-runs, loc.Best reports the prefix absent; it calls checkBestPathChange directly rather than through a received withdrawal (the receive path running the decision is 9-3's carrier) and carries no discrimination record, but its assertion is exact and fails if the no-candidate branch of checkRouteBestChange stopped calling removeLocRIB. Negatives (reactor/rfc4271_rs_replacement_test.go, split in 1d549b72cd, live bgp-rs/bgp-rib/bgp-adj-rib-in sessions): a second source's worse route is announced then withdrawn while the best stays feasible; TestRFC4271RouteServerStillFeasibleRouteStaysInLocRIB reads locrib.Default() behind a causal fence (bgp-rib stored B's marker sent after its withdrawal) and requires P still installed with A's NEXT_HOP, which confines removal to unfeasible routes; TestRFC4271RouteServerStillFeasibleRouteIsNotWithdrawn requires the client wire to keep A's route with one announcement and zero withdrawals, the wire consequence of the feasible route staying. Discrimination records verified for both negatives: mutant checkRouteBestChange 'newBest == nil' -> true reddens the Loc-RIB unit; mutant oweAnnouncement contest test -> true reddens the wire unit. Two negatives for one requirement are distinct observations (Loc-RIB, wire), not one assertion wearing two hats.
